meta_desc: GCSE History — interpretations and consequences of westward expansion 1840-95.
final_note: You weighed the West as triumph, tragedy and theft — and judged sources from both sides.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1893 historian Frederick Jackson Turner gave his Frontier Thesis.

He argued the frontier made Americans tough, democratic and independent. For many Americans, settling the West was a story of progress, courage and Manifest Destiny.

For Plains Indians it was a catastrophe.

Around 60 million buffalo were almost wiped out. Sioux and Cheyenne lost their land. Treaties were broken — like Fort Laramie in 1868. The Dawes Act of 1887 broke up shared reservations into private plots.

The Ghost Dance of 1889-90 promised the return of the buffalo and dead ancestors.

Soldiers feared a rising. Sitting Bull was killed in December 1890. Two weeks later came the Wounded Knee massacre. The Census declared the frontier closed in 1890.

mcqs.q: Why did the American colonies rebel against Britain?
options: Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
The colonists rebelled because they were heavily oppressed and impoverished.
Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Disputes over taxation without representation after the Seven Years' War, growing colonial identity, and British attempts to tighten imperial control on previously autonomous colonies.

mcqs.q: Did the Wall Street Crash cause the Great Depression?
options: The Wall Street Crash happened because the US joined WWII.
Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
The Wall Street Crash on its own caused the Great Depression.
It triggered it but the underlying causes were over-production, agricultural slump, weak banking regulation, and uneven wealth — the Crash exposed structural problems.
